subject: Request: Executive pricing variance & deferred billing for Heliotrix pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@heliotrix.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliotrix.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot ask: pricing variance + deferred billing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the cost breakdown you ran for our sample load. Heliotrix is ready to kick off a 3-month pilot (50k gen tokens/day average) but we have two commercial asks before legal signs the SOW:

1) A one-time uplift credit / variance to make the pilot economics comparable to our incumbent (we're asking for a 20% starter credit applied to the first 90 days).
2) Deferred billing until a formal go/no-go decision at the end of the pilot (invoice at net 30 after successful completion).

We attached the SOW draft for reference (Heliotrix_SOW_draft_v2.pdf). Can Redwood support either or both of these? If you need internal approvals, happy to provide a short business justification on our side.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships
Heliotrix, Inc.
attachments: HelioTrix_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 310KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pilot ask: pricing variance + deferred billing

Folks — forwarding a request from Heliotrix. Short summary: 3-month pilot, ~50k gen tokens/day expected, external wants 20% starter credit plus deferred billing until pilot completion. SOW attached.

I think this is a strategic pilot: Heliotrix is an AI-native imaging SaaS with strong enterprise sales motion (targeting clinical workflows) and they sign quickly if the tech and economics line up. We can win a multi-year committed deal if we make the pilot low friction.

Proposed internal ask for approval routing:
- One-time credit: 20% applied to host charges for first 90 days (total $X estimate in the workbook).
- Deferred billing: accept invoice after pilot completion (invoice N+30).
- Contingency: if pilot fails due to integration reasons on their side, credit is void.

Can you confirm whether we have precedent for deferred billing on pilots and what margin hit we can tolerate? Marcus — can you run quick margin sensitivity in the attached workbook? Aditya — would appreciate if you can route to VP/CFO track if it looks acceptable.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
--- Forwarded attachment: Heliotrix_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 310KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask: pricing variance + deferred billing

Marissa — thanks for flagging. High level thoughts:

- I’m supportive of a one-time promotional credit to lock the pilot, but we should cap the absolute dollar exposure and make the credit contingent on activation milestones.
- Deferred billing is acceptable on a case-by-case basis but requires finance sign-off (we need to track receivables and avoid large open credit).

Suggested guardrails to take to VP/CFO:
1) Starter credit = 20% of estimated hosting charges, capped at $40k total.
2) Apply credit as a one-time invoice line item that can be clawed back if the customer cancels for non-Redwood reasons.
3) Deferred billing: invoice at pilot close with net-30 payment terms; require PO or written procurement commitment beforehand.
4) Require SSO + SOC2 attestation before enabling production data flows.

Marcus — can you produce a 1-pager margin impact and the workbook numbers by EOD? If it looks within the cap, I’ll draft the exec memo to route to CFO (cc: finance) for a quick decision.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask: pricing variance + deferred billing

Aditya / Marissa — attached the sensitivity workbook (pricing_workbook.xlsx). Key notes:

- Baseline estimate (no credit): 3-month hosting = $160,000; average margin ~62%.
- 20% credit = reduces revenue by $32,000 (one-time), margin falls to ~57% (assuming hosting-only, excludes professional services).
- If we cap the credit at $40k we stay within a tolerable margin band for strategic pilots.
- Deferred billing increases DSO exposure by ~45 days on a $128k invoice (scenario dependent). Finance will want a PO or procurement acknowledgement before agreeing.

Proposed language for the exec memo (short):
"Approve one-time promotional credit of up to $40,000 (not to exceed 20% of estimated pilot hosting charges) for Heliotrix three-month pilot. Allow deferred billing with invoice issued at pilot close (net-30), contingent on receipt of PO and SOC2 attestation. Credit is void if customer cancels due to reasons attributable to customer integration failure."

I will prepare the formal memo and route to CFO (cc: finance ops) after you sign off on the cap. If you want, I’ll include quick P&L waterfall and attachment that shows sensitivity to token throughput.

Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB)
